newsitem.title: CHINA: China January trade surplus $1.71 bln-Customs.
newsitem.headline: China January trade surplus $1.71 bln-Customs.

text.p: China posted a trade surplus of $1.71 billion in January compared with a deficit of $938 million in January 1996, customs figures issued by the Xinhua news agency on Wednesday showed.
Note: figures in billions of U.S. dollars
Exports climbed by 27.5 percent in January compared with the year-ago period, the customs figures showed.
Imports were up by 1.2 percent year-on-year.
Exports of general products soared sharply while imports fell dramatically, the Xinhua news agency said. Trade in processed goods remained comparatively high, it said.
The rate of increase in imports of equipment by foreign-invested firms slowed, the report said.
However, for the first time trade by foreign-invested firms exceeded that by state-owned enterprises, it said.

This was a result of a long-term trend created by China's emphasis on encouraging mainly export-oriented foreign investment, said Jason Kwok, chief economist for China and Hong Kong at Citibank in Hong Kong.

China has long wanted to protect its domestic industry from foreign competition in its home market. But it has hinted it will in future allow foreign-invested firms more leeway to exploit the domestic market.

If that happens then the proportion of foreign trade held by foreign-funded firms could slip back, Kwok said, adding that faster payment by the government of export tax rebates would help state-owned exporters to boost their share.
The customs gave a preliminary breakdown of trade, saying exports of labour-intensive items accounted for 13.6 percent of the total while industrial products made up 86.4 percent.
Machinery and electronics remained the top export item followed by garments, it said.

In January, Hong Kong became China's second biggest trading partner, surpassing the United States, customs said. Japan remained China's biggest trading partner but trade slipped in January, it said without giving details.
